items.claim: Q2 2026 revenue guidance range given as $5.0B-$5.4B.
items.quote: revenue in the range of $5 billion to $5.4 billion
items.speaker: Rafael Lizardi

items.claim: Q2 2026 EPS guidance range given as $1.77-$2.05.
items.quote: earnings per share to be in the range of $1.77 to $2.05
items.speaker: Rafael Lizardi

items.claim: Q1 gross profit margin rose 210 basis points sequentially to 58% of revenue.
items.quote: gross profit margin increased 210 basis points
items.speaker: Rafael Lizardi

items.claim: CFO frames the long-term incremental (fall-through) gross margin on additional revenue at 75%-85%, excluding depreciation.
items.quote: fall-through that you should expect is in the 75% to 85%
items.speaker: Rafael Lizardi

items.claim: CFO reiterates 2026 depreciation guidance of $2.2B-$2.4B, unchanged from three months prior.
items.quote: No change to depreciation expectations for this year,
items.speaker: Rafael Lizardi

items.claim: CEO says it is likely analog pricing could rise in the second half of the year if strong demand persists.
items.quote: prices may go up in the second half of the year
items.speaker: Haviv Ilan

items.claim: CEO says TI's combination of portfolio breadth, supply ability, and U.S. manufacturing is a competitive advantage that is hard for rivals to replicate all at once.
items.quote: trying to replicate all -- in this case, all 3 is not easy
items.speaker: Haviv Ilan

items.claim: CEO states TI gained analog market share in 2025.
items.quote: we have gained share, of course, in analog in 2025
items.speaker: Haviv Ilan

items.quote: $2 billion to $3 billion of CapEx for this year
items.speaker: Rafael Lizardi

items.claim: Company returned $6 billion to shareholders via dividends and buybacks over the trailing 12 months.
items.quote: returned $6 billion to our owners in the past 12 months
items.speaker: Rafael Lizardi

items.claim: CEO says hitting $8 free cash flow per share for 2026 is very likely absent a repeat of last year's growth 'false start'.
items.quote: we'll easily be at $8 free cash flow per share for 2026
items.speaker: Haviv Ilan

items.claim: CEO describes TI's general-purpose analog portfolio as able to fill nearly every analog socket on a data center rack.
items.quote: We can fulfill, I would say, almost every analog socket
items.speaker: Haviv Ilan

items.claim: CEO notes TI has internalized most of its assembly-and-test supply chain.
items.quote: we've brought most of our supply internally
items.speaker: Haviv Ilan

items.claim: Management flags geopolitics and macro conditions as factors being watched heading into the second half.
items.quote: There is geopolitics. There is a macro that we are watching.
items.speaker: Haviv Ilan

items.claim: CEO flags tightness in the external outsourced assembly-and-test (OSAT) market.
items.quote: There is a tightness on the OSAT world.
items.speaker: Haviv Ilan

items.claim: CEO says Q1 automotive revenue was flat overall sequentially, with China down and rest-of-world up.
items.quote: China was down. The rest of the world was up.
items.speaker: Haviv Ilan

items.claim: CEO characterizes Q1 industrial strength as the broad tail of smaller customers waking up after a long slowdown.
items.quote: the tail starting to wake up again after a long hibernation
items.speaker: Haviv Ilan

items.claim: CEO announces TI's agreement to acquire Silicon Labs.
items.quote: we announced an agreement for TI to acquire Silicon Labs
items.speaker: Haviv Ilan

items.claim: CEO states the Silicon Labs acquisition is expected to close in the first half of 2027, subject to approvals.
items.quote: We expect the transaction to close in the first half of 2027
items.speaker: Haviv Ilan

qa_flags.question: Given how different March was and choppiness in autos (especially China), can you give color on what's assumed for industrial vs. automotive in the June quarter guide?
qa_flags.response_pattern: Haviv declines to split the guide by segment ('I won't break it out between the 2 but we see strength in both'), answering with qualitative automotive commentary instead of the numeric breakdown requested.

qa_flags.question: What percentage of your customers are on annual price contracts such that a pricing reset would more likely happen toward the end of the year/into next year?
qa_flags.response_pattern: Haviv does not give a percentage or contract-mix figure; he recaps general 2025/Q1 pricing trends and defers specifics, saying 'we'll report back during the July call.'

qa_flags.question: What are the puts and takes for the second half vs. first half given macro trends and memory price inflation, and how are fab loadings being managed?
qa_flags.response_pattern: Haviv gives no concrete second-half framework, repeating 'let's let 2Q play out and we'll call it as we see it' and citing last year's growth 'head fake' as the reason to withhold a view.
